data.title: Haleos Labs' (NSE:HALEOSLABS) Shareholders Have More To Worry About Than Only Soft Earnings
data.description:
Haleos Labs Limited's (NSE:HALEOSLABS) stock showed strength, with investors undeterred by its weak earnings report. While shareholders may be willing to overlook soft profit numbers, we believe that they should also be taking into account some other factors which may be cause for concern.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

A Closer Look At Haleos Labs' Earnings

In high finance, the key ratio used to measure how well a company converts reported profits into free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio (from cashflow). In plain english, this ratio subtracts FCF from net profit, and divides that number by the company's average operating assets over that period. You could think of the accrual ratio from cashflow as the 'non-FCF profit ratio'.

Therefore, it's actually considered a good thing when a company has a negative accrual ratio, but a bad thing if its accrual ratio is positive. While having an accrual ratio above zero is of little concern, we do think it's worth noting when a company has a relatively high accrual ratio. To quote a 2014 paper by Lewellen and Resutek, "firms with higher accruals tend to be less profitable in the future".

Haleos Labs has an accrual ratio of 0.23 for the year to September 2026. Unfortunately, that means its free cash flow fell significantly short of its reported profits. Even though it reported a profit of ₹129.5m, a look at free cash flow indicates it actually burnt through ₹612m in the last year. We saw that FCF was ₹262m a year ago though, so Haleos Labs has at least been able to generate positive FCF in the past. The good news for shareholders is that Haleos Labs' accrual ratio was much better last year, so this year's poor reading might simply be a case of a short term mismatch between profit and FCF. As a result, some shareholders may be looking for stronger cash conversion in the current year.

Our Take On Haleos Labs' Profit Performance

Haleos Labs didn't convert much of its profit to free cash flow in the last year, which some investors may consider rather suboptimal. Therefore, it seems possible to us that Haleos Labs' true underlying earnings power is actually less than its statutory profit. But on the bright side, its earnings per share have grown at an extremely impressive rate over the last three years. data.title: Revenue Beat: AFFIN Bank Berhad Exceeded Revenue Forecasts By 10% And Analysts Are Updating Their Estimates
data.description:
As you might know, AFFIN Bank Berhad (KLSE:AFFIN) just kicked off its latest third-quarter results with some very strong numbers. It was a positive result, with revenues and statutory earnings per share (EPS) both performing well. Revenues were 10% higher than the analysts had forecast, at RM691m, while EPS of RM0.043 beat analyst models by 2.8%. Following the result, the analysts have updated their earnings model, and it would be good to know whether they think there's been a strong change in the company's prospects, or if it's business as usual. We've gathered the most recent statutory forecasts to see whether the analysts have changed their earnings models, following these results.

Taking into account the latest results, the consensus forecast from AFFIN Bank Berhad's nine analysts is for revenues of RM2.80b in 2027. This reflects a decent 15% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Statutory earnings per share are predicted to ascend 20% to RM0.23. Before this earnings report, the analysts had been forecasting revenues of RM2.82b and earnings per share (EPS) of RM0.24 in 2027. The analysts seem to have become a little more negative on the business after the latest results, given the minor downgrade to their earnings per share numbers for next year.

View our latest analysis for AFFIN Bank Berhad

The average price target fell 9.3% to RM2.16, with reduced earnings forecasts clearly tied to a lower valuation estimate. There's another way to think about price targets though, and that's to look at the range of price targets put forward by analysts, because a wide range of estimates could suggest a diverse view on possible outcomes for the business. There are some variant perceptions on AFFIN Bank Berhad, with the most bullish analyst valuing it at RM2.50 and the most bearish at RM1.92 per share. This is a very narrow spread of estimates, implying either that AFFIN Bank Berhad is an easy company to value, or - more likely - the analysts are relying heavily on some key assumptions.

Of course, another way to look at these forecasts is to place them into context against the industry itself. We can infer from the latest estimates that forecasts expect a continuation of AFFIN Bank Berhad'shistorical trends, as the 12% annualised revenue growth to the end of 2027 is roughly in line with the 10% annual growth over the past five years. Compare this with the broader industry, which analyst estimates (in aggregate) suggest will see revenues grow 6.2% annually. So although AFFIN Bank Berhad is expected to maintain its revenue growth rate, it's definitely expected to grow faster than the wider industry.

The Bottom Line

The biggest concern is that the analysts reduced their earnings per share estimates, suggesting business headwinds could lay ahead for AFFIN Bank Berhad. Fortunately, they also reconfirmed their revenue numbers, suggesting that it's tracking in line with expectations. Additionally, our data suggests that revenue is expected to grow faster than the wider industry. The consensus price target fell measurably, with the analysts seemingly not reassured by the latest results, leading to a lower estimate of AFFIN Bank Berhad's future valuation.

data.title: There May Be Underlying Issues With The Quality Of Mochida Pharmaceutical's (TSE:4534) Earnings
data.description:
Mochida Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.'s (TSE:4534) stock was strong after they recently reported robust earnings. We did some analysis and think that investors are missing some details hidden beneath the profit numbers.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Zooming In On Mochida Pharmaceutical's Earnings

As finance nerds would already know, the accrual ratio from cashflow is a key measure for assessing how well a company's free cash flow (FCF) matches its profit. In plain english, this ratio subtracts FCF from net profit, and divides that number by the company's average operating assets over that period. You could think of the accrual ratio from cashflow as the 'non-FCF profit ratio'.

As a result, a negative accrual ratio is a positive for the company, and a positive accrual ratio is a negative. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

Mochida Pharmaceutical has an accrual ratio of 0.24 for the year to September 2026. We can therefore deduce that its free cash flow fell well short of covering its statutory profit. Even though it reported a profit of JP¥10.8b, a look at free cash flow indicates it actually burnt through JP¥14b in the last year. It's worth noting that Mochida Pharmaceutical generated positive FCF of JP¥2.8b a year ago, so at least they've done it in the past. Having said that, there is more to the story. We can see that unusual items have impacted its statutory profit, and therefore the accrual ratio.

See our latest analysis for Mochida Pharmaceutical

Note: we always recommend investors check balance sheet strength. Click here to be taken to our balance sheet analysis of Mochida Pharmaceutical.

The Impact Of Unusual Items On Profit

Given the accrual ratio, it's not overly surprising that Mochida Pharmaceutical's profit was boosted by unusual items worth JP¥989m in the last twelve months. While we like to see profit increases, we tend to be a little more cautious when unusual items have made a big contribution. We ran the numbers on most publicly listed companies worldwide, and it's very common for unusual items to be once-off in nature. And, after all, that's exactly what the accounting terminology implies. If Mochida Pharmaceutical doesn't see that contribution repeat, then all else being equal we'd expect its profit to drop over the current year.

Our Take On Mochida Pharmaceutical's Profit Performance

Summing up, Mochida Pharmaceutical received a nice boost to profit from unusual items, but could not match its paper profit with free cash flow. data.title: Should Vaccine Medium Launch Require Action From Thermo Fisher Scientific (TMO) Investors?
data.description:
• Thermo Fisher Scientific recently launched Gibco VaxEvo CD 293 Medium, a chemically defined, animal origin free solution for suspension HEK293 cultures that is designed to support high titer adenovirus production for vaccine developers across liquid and AGT formats.
  • The medium targets a practical bottleneck in adenovirus vaccine workflows by aiming to pair robust HEK293 cell growth with simplified, feed free upstream processes for human and animal health manufacturers.
  • Next, the focus shifts to what this new HEK293 vaccine medium could mean for Thermo Fisher Scientific broader investment narrative.

Thermo Fisher Scientific Investment Narrative Recap

To own Thermo Fisher Scientific, you need to believe the business can keep turning its large tools and services footprint into steadier earnings, even while academic and government demand stays muted. The analyst consensus narrative on Simply Wall St focuses on pharma and biotech customers, bioproduction and higher value instruments to do that heavy lifting. The new VaxEvo CD 293 Medium fits that story but appears incremental rather than a major factor for near term results.

The bigger near term swing still depends on how quickly funding-sensitive customers recover and how effectively Thermo Fisher Scientific executes its portfolio reshaping, including the microbiology divestiture. If funding remains softer than expected or divestiture proceeds and reinvestment underwhelm, the risk is that margin expansion and earnings growth prove harder to deliver than analysts currently include in their models.

Among the recent items, the quarterly dividend affirmation of US$0.47 a share is most relevant alongside VaxEvo. It indicates the board is comfortable returning cash while the firm invests in areas such as higher end media for HEK293 vaccine work, clinical trial logistics and bioproduction capacity. For you as a shareholder, that suggests a management team trying to balance reinvestment needs with regular cash returns.

The dividend itself is unlikely to move the stock by much, but it highlights capital allocation as one of the key execution levers from here, alongside M&A and debt management. If Thermo Fisher Scientific continues to fund product launches like VaxEvo, integrate deals such as Clario and Solventum and still support the payout, that combination could be more important for the medium term catalyst path than any single product launch.

Thermo Fisher Scientific's current narrative assumes revenue of US$56.1b and earnings of US$10.7b by 2029, built on 5.8% yearly top line growth and an earnings increase of about US$3.6b from US$7.1b today.
